theme: Suspension bridges: the roadway is hung from vertical hangers attached to main cables draped over towers and anchored at each end.
decoy: Famous long-span road bridges held up by towers and cables

members.title: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
members.description: Span linking Kobe to Awaji Island across a strait prone to typhoons.

members.title: Humber Bridge
members.description: Crossing of a wide estuary in East Yorkshire, opened in 1981.

members.title: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge
members.description: Double-level span joining Staten Island and Brooklyn at the mouth of New York Harbor.

members.title: Great Belt East Bridge
members.description: Danish span carrying a motorway between Zealand and the islet of Sprogo.

members.title: Tsing Ma Bridge
members.description: Road and rail span on the route to Hong Kong's airport.

members.title: Mackinac Bridge
members.description: Five-mile crossing joining the two peninsulas of Michigan.

members.title: George Washington Bridge
members.description: Double-deck Hudson River crossing between Upper Manhattan and Fort Lee.

members.title: Forth Road Bridge
members.description: Motorway span in Scotland beside a famous red railway bridge.

members.title: Lions Gate Bridge
members.description: Green-painted crossing from Vancouver's Stanley Park to the North Shore.

intruders.title: Millau Viaduct
intruders.description: Span on slender piers carrying a motorway high over the Tarn valley in France.
intruders.why: A cable-stayed bridge: straight stays run from each pylon directly to the deck, with no main cables. Its fans of cables make it look like a suspension design.

intruders.title: Oresund Bridge
intruders.description: Road and rail span linking Copenhagen and Malmo by way of an island and tunnel.
intruders.why: Its main span is cable-stayed, with stays running straight from the pylons to the deck and no main cables. It is a long Danish strait crossing like the Great Belt East Bridge, which is a suspension bridge.

intruders.title: Pont de Normandie
intruders.description: Span over the Seine estuary between Le Havre and Honfleur.
intruders.why: A cable-stayed bridge with inverted-Y pylons and no main cables, though its long span and tall towers read as a suspension bridge.

theme: Cathedrals built in the Gothic style, with pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses.
decoy: Great historic cathedrals of Europe

members.title: Notre-Dame de Paris
members.description: Twin-towered cathedral on the Ile de la Cite with famous rose windows.

members.title: Chartres Cathedral
members.description: Cathedral southwest of Paris famed for its medieval stained glass and mismatched spires.

members.title: Reims Cathedral
members.description: Cathedral where French kings were traditionally crowned, home to a smiling angel carving.

members.title: Amiens Cathedral
members.description: Picardy cathedral with a vast nave and a labyrinth inlaid in its floor.

members.title: Salisbury Cathedral
members.description: English cathedral with a soaring spire, holding an original copy of Magna Carta.

members.title: Milan Cathedral
members.description: Pale marble cathedral bristling with spires and statues in Lombardy's capital.

members.title: Seville Cathedral
members.description: Andalusian cathedral whose bell tower began life as a minaret.

members.title: York Minster
members.description: Northern English cathedral with a great east window of medieval glass.

intruders.title: St Paul's Cathedral
intruders.description: London cathedral with a great dome, rebuilt after the fire of 1666.
intruders.why: Christopher Wren's English Baroque design, with round arches and a classical dome. Its medieval predecessor, Old St Paul's, was Gothic.

intruders.title: Pisa Cathedral
intruders.description: Marble cathedral in Tuscany beside a famously tilting bell tower.
intruders.why: Pisan Romanesque, with round arches and an arcaded marble facade and no flying buttresses. It is medieval, which makes it look Gothic.

intruders.title: Speyer Cathedral
intruders.description: Imperial cathedral on the Rhine where Salian emperors are buried.
intruders.why: A major Romanesque church with round arches and massive walls. It is a medieval cathedral of the same scale as the Gothic ones.

theme: Buildings designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.
decoy: Landmark American houses and buildings of the early and mid twentieth century

members.title: Fallingwater
members.description: House cantilevered over a waterfall on Bear Run in Pennsylvania.

members.title: Robie House
members.description: Long, low brick house with sweeping eaves on Chicago's South Side.

members.title: Unity Temple
members.description: Concrete Unitarian church in Oak Park, Illinois, lit by skylights.

members.title: Johnson Wax Headquarters
members.description: Office in Racine, Wisconsin, with slender mushroom-shaped columns and glass tubing.

members.title: Marin County Civic Center
members.description: Long blue-roofed government complex bridging hills north of San Francisco.

members.title: Hollyhock House
members.description: Los Angeles house for an oil heiress, decorated with stylized flowers.

members.title: Price Tower
members.description: Nineteen-story tower in Bartlesville, Oklahoma, with copper-trimmed floors.

members.title: Ennis House
members.description: Los Angeles house built of patterned concrete blocks with a Mayan feel.

members.title: Darwin D. Martin House
members.description: Buffalo estate of linked horizontal pavilions for a soap company executive.

intruders.title: Gamble House
intruders.description: Pasadena house of dark timber and deep eaves for a soap company heir.
intruders.why: Designed by the brothers Greene & Greene in 1908. Its horizontal lines and craftsmanship often get it mistaken for a Wright house.

intruders.title: Kaufmann Desert House
intruders.description: Flat-roofed glass and steel house in Palm Springs for a Pittsburgh store owner.
intruders.why: Designed by Richard Neutra in 1946 for Edgar Kaufmann, the same client who commissioned Fallingwater from Wright.

theme: Skyscrapers designed in the Art Deco style.
decoy: Early American skyscrapers built before the Second World War

members.title: Chrysler Building
members.description: Manhattan tower crowned by stainless-steel sunbursts and eagle gargoyles.

members.title: Empire State Building
members.description: Limestone Midtown tower with a mooring mast for airships at its top.

members.title: Chanin Building
members.description: Midtown office tower near Grand Central with a bronze frieze at its base.

members.title: Guardian Building
members.description: Detroit bank headquarters clad in orange brick and bright tilework.

members.title: Fisher Building
members.description: Detroit office tower with a gilded roof and a painted three-story arcade.

members.title: Chicago Board of Trade Building
members.description: LaSalle Street tower topped by an aluminum statue of Ceres.

members.title: Los Angeles City Hall
members.description: White civic tower with a pyramid-shaped top in downtown Los Angeles.

members.title: Carew Tower
members.description: Cincinnati office and hotel complex from 1930 with an observation deck.

intruders.title: Woolworth Building
intruders.description: Terracotta-clad Lower Manhattan tower from 1913 with a copper pyramid top.
intruders.why: Neo-Gothic, with pointed arches and tracery. It predates the arrival of Art Deco in the 1920s but is a classic early skyscraper.

intruders.title: Wrigley Building
intruders.description: White terracotta clock tower on Chicago's Michigan Avenue beside the river.
intruders.why: A 1920s revival design modeled on the Giralda in Seville. It dates from the Art Deco years but not the style.

intruders.title: Flatiron Building
intruders.description: Wedge-shaped office tower at the corner of Fifth Avenue and Broadway.
intruders.why: A Beaux-Arts design completed in 1902, decades before Art Deco. It is a famous early New York tower.

theme: Structures built to house the remains of the dead.
decoy: Grand commemorative monuments

members.title: Taj Mahal
members.description: White marble domed monument on the Yamuna River at Agra.

members.title: Castel Sant'Angelo
members.description: Cylindrical Roman monument beside the Tiber, later a papal fortress.

members.title: Great Pyramid of Giza
members.description: Limestone monument for the pharaoh Khufu on the Giza plateau.

members.title: Gur-e-Amir
members.description: Timurid monument in Samarkand with a ribbed turquoise dome.

members.title: Ming Xiaoling
members.description: Monumental complex for the Hongwu Emperor on Purple Mountain in Nanjing.

members.title: General Grant National Memorial
members.description: Granite domed monument on Riverside Drive in Manhattan honoring a Civil War general.

members.title: Itimad-ud-Daulah
members.description: Agra monument of inlaid white marble often called the Baby Taj.

members.title: Gol Gumbaz
members.description: Bijapur monument with a vast dome and a whispering gallery.

intruders.title: Lincoln Memorial
intruders.description: Marble temple on the National Mall enclosing a seated statue of a president.
intruders.why: A memorial only: Lincoln is buried in Springfield, Illinois. Its temple form resembles the grand mausoleums.

intruders.title: Shrine of Remembrance
intruders.description: Melbourne war monument modeled on the ancient Mausoleum at Halicarnassus.
intruders.why: Holds no remains. It honors Australians who served in war, even though its design copies a famous tomb.

intruders.title: Albert Memorial
intruders.description: Gothic canopy in Kensington Gardens sheltering a gilded seated prince.
intruders.why: Prince Albert is buried in the Royal Mausoleum at Frogmore, Windsor. This canopy is a memorial only.

theme: Castles built as genuine military fortifications.
decoy: Famous castles

members.title: Edinburgh Castle
members.description: Complex on an extinct volcanic crag above Scotland's capital.

members.title: Windsor Castle
members.description: Royal residence in Berkshire begun under William the Conqueror.

members.title: Tower of London
members.description: Norman keep and walled complex beside the Thames that houses the Crown Jewels.

members.title: Krak des Chevaliers
members.description: Crusader-era complex on a hilltop in western Syria.

members.title: Alcazar of Segovia
members.description: Spanish royal complex on a rocky prow above two rivers.

members.title: Malbork Castle
members.description: Brick complex of the Teutonic Knights on the Nogat River in Poland.

members.title: Himeji Castle
members.description: White-plastered Japanese complex nicknamed the White Heron.

members.title: Dover Castle
members.description: Clifftop complex above the Channel port, with a great square keep.

members.title: Conwy Castle
members.description: Medieval complex in North Wales with eight great towers.

intruders.title: Neuschwanstein Castle
intruders.description: Turreted Bavarian hilltop residence built for King Ludwig II.
intruders.why: A 19th-century Romantic palace (1869-86) with no defensive purpose. It is the archetypal fairy-tale castle.

intruders.title: Chateau de Chambord
intruders.description: Loire Valley residence with a double-helix staircase and a skyline of turrets.
intruders.why: Built as a hunting lodge for Francis I. Its towers are for show, not defense.

intruders.title: Hearst Castle
intruders.description: Hilltop estate on the California coast with twin towers and a Roman-style pool.
intruders.why: A 20th-century mansion designed by Julia Morgan for William Randolph Hearst. It is a castle in name only.

theme: Buildings deliberately designed in the shape of an everyday object or animal.
decoy: Buildings that look like familiar things

members.title: Longaberger Basket Building
members.description: Seven-story Ohio office block that looks like a picnic basket with handles.

members.title: Big Duck
members.description: Long Island farm shop that looks like a white duck.

members.title: Lucy the Elephant
members.description: Six-story New Jersey seaside structure that looks like an elephant.

members.title: Haines Shoe House
members.description: Pennsylvania house that looks like a giant work boot.

members.title: Teapot Dome Service Station
members.description: Washington State filling station that looks like a teapot.

members.title: Hood Milk Bottle
members.description: Boston waterfront snack stand that looks like a milk bottle.

members.title: Dog Bark Park Inn
members.description: Idaho guesthouse that looks like a giant beagle.

members.title: Piano House
members.description: Building in Huainan, China, that looks like a grand piano beside a violin.

intruders.title: The Gherkin
intruders.description: Rounded glass office tower in the City of London that looks like a pickle.
intruders.why: Foster's form for 30 St Mary Axe came from wind and energy concerns. The pickle is a nickname, not a design intent.

intruders.title: CCTV Headquarters
intruders.description: Looping angular tower in Beijing that looks like a pair of trousers.
intruders.why: OMA's loop is a structural and programmatic concept. 'Big Pants' is a popular nickname, not the design brief.

theme: Brutalist buildings: massive, blocky forms in raw, exposed concrete.
decoy: Postwar buildings of bare concrete

members.title: Barbican Estate
members.description: Concrete housing and arts complex in the City of London with three towers and a lake.

members.title: Boston City Hall
members.description: Top-heavy concrete civic building on a sloping brick plaza.

members.title: Trellick Tower
members.description: West London housing tower with a separate lift and service shaft.

members.title: Royal National Theatre
members.description: South Bank concrete theatre complex of stacked terraces beside Waterloo Bridge.

members.title: Geisel Library
members.description: Faceted concrete university library in San Diego perched on angled pillars.

members.title: Rudolph Hall
members.description: Yale's corduroy-textured concrete art and architecture building in New Haven.

members.title: Robarts Library
members.description: Triangular concrete University of Toronto library nicknamed Fort Book.

members.title: Preston Bus Station
members.description: Lancashire transport hub with curved concrete balcony edges on its car park decks.

members.title: Park Hill
members.description: Hillside Sheffield housing estate with wide streets in the sky.

intruders.title: TWA Flight Center
intruders.description: Wing-roofed concrete terminal at JFK Airport in New York.
intruders.why: Eero Saarinen's expressionist thin-shell design: sweeping, bird-like curves rather than Brutalism's heavy, blocky massing.

intruders.title: Dulles Airport Main Terminal
intruders.description: Concrete hall near Washington with a roof slung between tilted pillars.
intruders.why: Saarinen's expressionist design with a suspended, curving roof. It is sculptural and light, not Brutalist.

theme: Stepped pyramids: built as a stack of receding tiers or terraces rather than with smooth faces.
decoy: Ancient pyramids and pyramid-shaped monuments

members.title: Pyramid of Djoser
members.description: Egyptian royal monument at Saqqara designed by Imhotep.

members.title: Ziggurat of Ur
members.description: Mud-brick temple platform of the Sumerian moon god in southern Iraq.

members.title: El Castillo
members.description: Maya temple to Kukulcan at Chichen Itza with a staircase on each side.

members.title: Pyramid of the Sun
members.description: Great monument on the Avenue of the Dead at Teotihuacan.

members.title: Borobudur
members.description: Ninth-century Buddhist monument in Central Java lined with relief panels.

members.title: Chogha Zanbil
members.description: Elamite brick temple complex in southwestern Iran.

members.title: Tikal Temple I
members.description: Maya funerary monument in the Guatemalan rainforest topped by a roof comb.

members.title: Pyramid of the Magician
members.description: Maya monument at Uxmal with an unusual oval base.

members.title: Prasat Thom
members.description: Khmer temple monument at Koh Ker in northern Cambodia.

intruders.title: Red Pyramid
intruders.description: Egyptian royal monument at Dahshur named for the color of its stone.
intruders.why: A true smooth-sided pyramid built for Sneferu, the first successful one. It is from the same era as the stepped Egyptian ones.

intruders.title: Pyramid of Cestius
intruders.description: Marble-clad Roman monument beside the Porta San Paolo in Rome.
intruders.why: Its steep faces are smooth, imitating Egyptian and Nubian pyramids. It is ancient and pyramidal, with no steps.

theme: Structures built during Roman rule of their site, as opposed to earlier Greek work.
decoy: Ruins of Greek and Roman classical antiquity

members.title: Colosseum
members.description: Oval arena of travertine and concrete in the heart of Rome.

members.title: Pont du Gard
members.description: Three-tiered arched water bridge over the Gardon River in southern France.

members.title: Baths of Caracalla
members.description: Vast bathing complex ruins south of the city center in Rome.

members.title: Arch of Titus
members.description: Single-bay marble arch on the Via Sacra showing a triumphal procession.

members.title: Aqueduct of Segovia
members.description: Double-arched granite water channel striding through a Castilian city.

members.title: Library of Celsus
members.description: Two-story marble facade of a library in Ephesus, western Turkey.

members.title: Odeon of Herodes Atticus
members.description: Stone theatre on the slope of the Athenian Acropolis.

members.title: Hadrian's Wall
members.description: Stone frontier barrier running across northern England.

members.title: Theatre of Orange
members.description: Open-air theatre in Provence with its huge stage wall intact.

intruders.title: Temples of Paestum
intruders.description: Three stone temples on a coastal plain south of Salerno in Italy.
intruders.why: Built by Greek colonists of Poseidonia in the 6th and 5th centuries BC, before Rome took the city in 273 BC. They stand in Italy, which makes them look Roman.

intruders.title: Temple of Concordia
intruders.description: Stone temple on a ridge above the city of Agrigento in Sicily.
intruders.why: Built around 440-430 BC by the Greek city of Akragas. It stands in Italy but predates Roman rule.

theme: Buildings designed by Antoni Gaudi.
decoy: Landmarks of Catalan Modernisme architecture

members.title: Casa Batllo
members.description: Passeig de Gracia house in Barcelona with a scaly roof and bone-like balconies.

members.title: Casa Mila
members.description: Undulating stone apartment block nicknamed La Pedrera, with warrior-like chimneys.

members.title: Park Guell
members.description: Hillside park with a mosaic salamander and a serpentine tiled bench.

members.title: Palau Guell
members.description: Town mansion off La Rambla with parabolic-arched entrances and colorful chimneys.

members.title: Casa Vicens
members.description: Summer house in Gracia covered in green and white tiles with marigold motifs.

members.title: El Capricho
members.description: Villa in Comillas, Cantabria, with a slender tower clad in sunflower tiles.

members.title: Bellesguard
members.description: Stone villa on the slopes of Tibidabo in Barcelona, built on a medieval royal site.

members.title: Casa Calvet
members.description: Eixample apartment building with a baroque-influenced stone facade.

members.title: Crypt of Colonia Guell
members.description: Church crypt in a textile colony, with leaning basalt and brick pillars.

intruders.title: Casa Amatller
intruders.description: Passeig de Gracia house in Barcelona with a stepped gable facade of colored tiles.
intruders.why: Designed by Josep Puig i Cadafalch. It stands next door to Casa Batllo on the same block.

intruders.title: Palau de la Musica Catalana
intruders.description: Barcelona concert hall with a stained-glass skylight and mosaic-covered columns.
intruders.why: Designed by Lluis Domenech i Montaner, a Modernisme contemporary of Gaudi.

intruders.title: Hospital de Sant Pau
intruders.description: Barcelona garden complex of tiled pavilions linked by tunnels.
intruders.why: Designed by Lluis Domenech i Montaner. It is often visited alongside the Sagrada Familia nearby.

theme: Buildings whose outer colonnade uses the Doric order.
decoy: Greek temples and Greek Revival buildings

members.title: Parthenon
members.description: Marble temple of Athena crowning the Athenian Acropolis.

members.title: Temple of Hephaestus
members.description: Well-preserved marble temple overlooking the Agora of Athens.

members.title: Temple of Aphaia
members.description: Hilltop limestone temple on the island of Aegina.

members.title: Temple of Poseidon at Sounion
members.description: Cliff-top marble temple at the southern tip of Attica.

members.title: Temple of Segesta
members.description: Unfinished temple standing alone in the hills of western Sicily.

members.title: Temple of Zeus at Olympia
members.description: Ruined temple that once housed a giant gold-and-ivory statue.

members.title: Brandenburg Gate
members.description: Neoclassical gateway in Berlin topped by a four-horse chariot.

members.title: Walhalla
members.description: Hall of fame for German worthies, a temple above the Danube near Regensburg.

intruders.title: Erechtheion
intruders.description: Marble temple on the Athenian Acropolis with a porch of maidens.
intruders.why: Its colonnades are Ionic, and its famous porch uses caryatids. It shares the Acropolis with the Doric Parthenon.

intruders.title: Temple of Athena Nike
intruders.description: Small marble temple on a bastion at the entrance to the Athenian Acropolis.
intruders.why: An Ionic temple. It stands a few steps from the Doric Parthenon and Propylaea.

intruders.title: Maison Carree
intruders.description: Well-preserved Roman temple in the center of Nimes.
intruders.why: Its columns are Corinthian. It is a classical temple with the same colonnaded form.

theme: Structures dismantled and re-erected on a different site from the one where they were first built.
decoy: Famous historic structures that now draw crowds of visitors

members.title: John Rennie's London Bridge
members.description: Granite arch bridge of five spans, opened in 1831.

members.title: Temple of Dendur
members.description: Small Nubian sandstone temple from the reign of the emperor Augustus.

members.title: Abu Simbel temples
members.description: Twin rock temples of Ramesses II with four colossal seated statues.

members.title: Temple of Kalabsha
members.description: Large Nubian sandstone temple to the local god Mandulis.

members.title: Temple of Debod
members.description: Small Nubian temple to Amun and Isis, begun in the second century BC.

members.title: Temple of Isis at Philae
members.description: Ptolemaic temple of Isis with a great pylon and a riverside kiosk.

members.title: St Mary Aldermanbury
members.description: Wren church from the City of London, gutted in the Blitz.

members.title: Ancient Spanish Monastery
members.description: Twelfth-century Cistercian cloister from Sacramenia in the province of Segovia.

members.title: Agecroft Hall
members.description: Tudor manor house of timber and brick from Lancashire.

intruders.title: Tower Bridge
intruders.description: Victorian bridge with twin Gothic towers and lifting roadways over the Thames.
intruders.why: Never moved from London. A persistent myth says the American who bought Rennie's London Bridge thought he was getting Tower Bridge.

intruders.title: Temple of Edfu
intruders.description: Ptolemaic sandstone temple of Horus with a towering pylon and granite shrine.
intruders.why: Still stands where it was built, north of Aswan and above the reach of Lake Nasser. It is a Ptolemaic temple like Philae and Kalabsha, which were moved.

theme: Landmark buildings that have been demolished.
decoy: Celebrated stations, towers, and complexes of the late nineteenth and twentieth centuries

members.title: Pennsylvania Station
members.description: Beaux-Arts Manhattan rail terminal with a waiting room modeled on Roman baths.

members.title: Kowloon Walled City
members.description: Dense Hong Kong enclave of interlocking high-rise blocks with no planning oversight.

members.title: Pruitt-Igoe
members.description: Public housing complex of thirty-three eleven-story slabs in St. Louis.

members.title: Larkin Administration Building
members.description: Buffalo mail-order company headquarters with a skylit atrium, by Frank Lloyd Wright.

members.title: Singer Building
members.description: Beaux-Arts office tower in Lower Manhattan with a bulbous mansard crown.

members.title: Euston Arch
members.description: Doric gateway at the entrance to a London railway terminus.

members.title: Nakagin Capsule Tower
members.description: Tokyo tower of prefabricated pod rooms plugged into two concrete cores.

members.title: Chicago Stock Exchange Building
members.description: Louis Sullivan office building in the Loop with an ornate arched entrance.

intruders.title: Grand Central Terminal
intruders.description: Beaux-Arts Manhattan rail terminal with a celestial ceiling over its main concourse.
intruders.why: Threatened by a 1960s tower plan, it was saved by New York's landmarks law, upheld by the Supreme Court in 1978. It is the great Manhattan counterpart of the lost Penn Station.

intruders.title: Battersea Power Station
intruders.description: Brick London power station with four white chimneys beside the Thames.
intruders.why: Decommissioned in 1983 and left derelict for decades, but restored and redeveloped rather than torn down.

theme: Structures whose main frame is built of timber.
decoy: Celebrated temples, pagodas, churches, and bridges

members.title: Horyu-ji
members.description: Seventh-century Buddhist temple complex near Nara with a five-story pagoda.

members.title: Todai-ji Daibutsuden
members.description: Nara hall enclosing a colossal bronze seated Buddha.

members.title: Urnes Stave Church
members.description: Medieval Norwegian church with intricately carved animal ornament.

members.title: Kizhi Church of the Transfiguration
members.description: Russian island church crowned by twenty-two onion domes.

members.title: Fogong Temple Pagoda
members.description: Octagonal pagoda at Yingxian in Shanxi, raised in 1056.

members.title: Kapellbrucke
members.description: Covered footbridge in Lucerne with painted panels under its roof.

members.title: Metropol Parasol
members.description: Giant waffle-like canopy over a square in Seville.

members.title: Mjostarnet
members.description: Eighteen-story mixed-use tower on the shore of Lake Mjosa in Norway.

members.title: Sanjusangen-do
members.description: Long Kyoto hall housing 1,001 statues of the goddess Kannon.

intruders.title: Iron Pagoda
intruders.description: Slender eleventh-century pagoda in Kaifeng with a rust-brown glazed skin.
intruders.why: Built of brick sheathed in glazed tiles; the 'iron' name refers only to its color. It echoes the Fogong pagoda in age and form.

intruders.title: Great Wild Goose Pagoda
intruders.description: Square seven-story pagoda in Xi'an built to hold Buddhist scriptures.
intruders.why: A brick masonry pagoda. It is a Tang-dynasty Buddhist landmark like the Japanese temples.

theme: Movable bridges: all or part of the span opens to let vessels pass.
decoy: Distinctive bridges over urban waterways

members.title: Gateshead Millennium Bridge
members.description: Curved pedestrian and cycle crossing on the Tyne, dating from 2001.

members.title: Rolling Bridge
members.description: Short footbridge over a canal inlet at Paddington Basin, London.

members.title: Erasmus Bridge
members.description: Asymmetric white crossing over the Maas in Rotterdam, nicknamed The Swan.

members.title: Pegasus Bridge
members.description: Canal crossing at Benouville in Normandy, famous from D-Day.

members.title: Magere Brug
members.description: White crossing over the Amstel in Amsterdam, strung with lights at night.

members.title: Puente de la Mujer
members.description: Pedestrian crossing in Puerto Madero, Buenos Aires, with a single angled mast.

members.title: Aerial Lift Bridge
members.description: Steel crossing over the canal entrance to Duluth harbor on Lake Superior.

members.title: Steel Bridge
members.description: Double-deck Willamette River crossing in Portland carrying rail and road.

members.title: Galata Bridge
members.description: Istanbul crossing over the Golden Horn lined with fishermen and restaurants.

intruders.title: Puente del Alamillo
intruders.description: Crossing in Seville with a single angled mast leaning back over the land.
intruders.why: A fixed cable-stayed bridge. Calatrava also designed the Puente de la Mujer, which swings open.

intruders.title: Tyne Bridge
intruders.description: Green steel arch crossing on the Tyne linking Newcastle and Gateshead.
intruders.why: A fixed arch bridge. It stands a short way upriver from the tilting Gateshead Millennium Bridge.

theme: Cities planned and built from scratch to be a seat of government.
decoy: Capital cities

members.title: Brasilia
members.description: Brazilian capital on the central plateau with Niemeyer's modernist ministries.

members.title: Canberra
members.description: Australian capital set around the artificial Lake Burley Griffin.

members.title: Washington, D.C.
members.description: Capital on the Potomac with radiating avenues and a long central Mall.

members.title: Islamabad
members.description: Pakistani capital at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

members.title: Abuja
members.description: Nigerian capital beneath the granite monolith of Aso Rock.

members.title: Putrajaya
members.description: Malaysian administrative capital with a pink-domed mosque beside a lake.

members.title: Belmopan
members.description: Small inland capital of Belize, away from the hurricane-prone coast.

members.title: Chandigarh
members.description: Shared capital of Punjab and Haryana with a Le Corbusier civic complex.

members.title: Gaborone
members.description: Capital of Botswana near the South African border.

intruders.title: Ottawa
intruders.description: Canadian capital with Gothic Revival parliament buildings above a river.
intruders.why: Grew from Bytown, a lumber and canal town, before it was chosen as capital in 1857.

intruders.title: Ankara
intruders.description: Turkish capital on the Anatolian plateau with a hilltop citadel.
intruders.why: The ancient city of Ancyra, inhabited for millennia. Its 1920s plan extended an existing city rather than founding a new one.

theme: Buildings designed by Frank Gehry.
decoy: Sculptural, curving contemporary buildings clad in metal or glass

members.title: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
members.description: Titanium-clad art museum curving along the Nervion river in Spain.

members.title: Walt Disney Concert Hall
members.description: Concert hall with stainless-steel sails on Grand Avenue in Los Angeles.

members.title: Fondation Louis Vuitton
members.description: Art museum of billowing glass sails in the Bois de Boulogne, Paris.

members.title: Weisman Art Museum
members.description: Brushed-steel university museum overlooking the Mississippi in Minneapolis.

members.title: Museum of Pop Culture
members.description: Crumpled, multicolored metal museum beside the monorail in Seattle.

members.title: 8 Spruce Street
members.description: Lower Manhattan residential tower with a rippling stainless-steel skin.

members.title: Stata Center
members.description: Tilting, colliding computer science and linguistics building at MIT.

members.title: Jay Pritzker Pavilion
members.description: Outdoor bandshell in Chicago's Millennium Park with a steel trellis over the lawn.

members.title: Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health
members.description: Las Vegas medical center with a wavy lattice of steel and windows.

intruders.title: Heydar Aliyev Center
intruders.description: Flowing white cultural center in Baku without a single sharp angle.
intruders.why: Designed by Zaha Hadid Architects. Its sweeping curved surfaces resemble Gehry's work.

intruders.title: Imperial War Museum North
intruders.description: Museum on the Manchester Ship Canal clad in aluminum shards.
intruders.why: Designed by Daniel Libeskind. Its fractured metal forms look like Gehry's.

theme: Buildings whose design was selected through an architectural competition.
decoy: Major civic and cultural landmarks

members.title: Centre Pompidou
members.description: Paris arts center with its pipes, ducts, and escalators on the outside.

members.title: Tribune Tower
members.description: Neo-Gothic Chicago newspaper tower with flying buttresses at its crown.

members.title: Vietnam Veterans Memorial
members.description: Black granite V-shaped wall of names on the National Mall.

members.title: Oslo Opera House
members.description: White sloping roof you can walk up from the waterfront in Norway's capital.

members.title: Grande Arche
members.description: Hollow white cube of a monument at La Defense on the Paris axis.

members.title: Jewish Museum Berlin
members.description: Zigzag zinc-clad museum with slashed windows and empty voids.

members.title: Palais Garnier
members.description: Opulent Second Empire opera house in Paris with a grand staircase.

members.title: Parc de la Villette
members.description: Paris park scattered with red steel follies on a grid.

members.title: Reichstag Building
members.description: German parliament in Berlin crowned by a glass cupola with a spiral ramp.

intruders.title: Louvre Pyramid
intruders.description: Glass and steel pyramid entrance in the main courtyard of a Paris museum.
intruders.why: President Mitterrand chose I. M. Pei directly in 1983, with no competition. It was one of the Paris Grands Projets, several of which were competition winners.

intruders.title: Kimbell Art Museum
intruders.description: Fort Worth art museum of long concrete vaults lit by slots of daylight.
intruders.why: Director Richard Brown chose Louis Kahn directly in 1966, with no design competition. It is a celebrated cultural landmark like the members.

theme: Great churches that are not cathedrals: none is the seat of a bishop.
decoy: Famous grand churches

members.title: St Peter's Basilica
members.description: Vatican church beneath Michelangelo's dome, facing Bernini's colonnade.

members.title: Sagrada Familia
members.description: Barcelona church of many spires, begun in 1882.

members.title: Sacre-Coeur
members.description: White travertine domed church crowning Montmartre in Paris.

members.title: Sainte-Chapelle
members.description: Gothic royal chapel in Paris walled with stained glass.

members.title: King's College Chapel
members.description: Late Gothic chapel in Cambridge with a vast fan vault.

members.title: Hallgrimskirkja
members.description: Reykjavik church with a concrete tower evoking basalt columns.

members.title: Santa Maria Maggiore
members.description: Papal basilica on the Esquiline Hill with early Christian mosaics.

members.title: Grundtvig's Church
members.description: Copenhagen church of yellow brick with an organ-pipe facade.

members.title: Sistine Chapel
members.description: Vatican chapel with a frescoed ceiling, used for papal conclaves.

intruders.title: St Mark's Basilica
intruders.description: Venetian church of five domes and gold mosaics on its piazza.
intruders.why: It has been the cathedral of the Patriarch of Venice since 1807. It began as the doge's chapel, which is why it is often assumed not to be one.

intruders.title: San Giovanni in Laterano
intruders.description: Papal basilica in Rome with a facade of giant statues of Christ and saints.
intruders.why: The cathedral of Rome, where the pope sits as Bishop of Rome; it outranks St Peter's. It is called a basilica, like the other Roman churches.

theme: Structures whose chief designer died before they were completed.
decoy: Famous landmarks completed from the mid nineteenth to the early twenty-first century

members.title: Brooklyn Bridge
members.description: Granite-towered crossing of the East River opened in 1883.

members.title: Palace of Westminster
members.description: Gothic Revival riverside home of the UK Parliament with its clock tower.

members.title: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
members.description: Spiraling white art museum on Fifth Avenue opened in 1959.

members.title: Gateway Arch
members.description: Stainless-steel arch on the Mississippi riverfront in St. Louis.

members.title: Scottish Parliament Building
members.description: Holyrood complex of upturned-boat roofs and odd window shapes.

members.title: Royal Courts of Justice
members.description: Victorian Gothic law courts on the Strand in London.

members.title: National Parliament House, Dhaka
members.description: Concrete and marble assembly complex with geometric cutouts, set in a lake.

members.title: Washington Monument
members.description: Marble obelisk at the center of the National Mall.

intruders.title: Sydney Opera House
intruders.description: Harbourside performing arts center crowned by white shells.
intruders.why: Utzon resigned in 1966 and never saw it finished, but he lived until 2008, long after its 1973 opening.

intruders.title: Golden Gate Bridge
intruders.description: International-orange crossing at the entrance to San Francisco Bay.
intruders.why: Chief engineer Joseph Strauss saw it open in May 1937 and died a year later.

theme: Buildings officially named for their own postal address.
decoy: Modern towers known by a number

members.title: 432 Park Avenue
members.description: Slender concrete residential tower with a grid of square windows in Midtown Manhattan.

members.title: 56 Leonard Street
members.description: Tribeca residential tower of cantilevered glass boxes stacked like a game of Jenga.

members.title: One Canada Square
members.description: Canary Wharf office tower with a pyramid top and a flashing aircraft light.

members.title: 20 Fenchurch Street
members.description: London office tower that widens toward the top, with a sky garden.

members.title: 22 Bishopsgate
members.description: Broad glass office tower in the eastern cluster of the City of London.

members.title: 70 Pine Street
members.description: Lower Manhattan tower built for an oil company, with a lantern crown.

members.title: 111 West 57th Street
members.description: Ultra-thin residential tower on Billionaires' Row with terracotta-faced flanks.

members.title: One Vanderbilt
members.description: Tapering glass supertall beside Grand Central with a stepped, faceted crown.

intruders.title: Tower 42
intruders.description: City of London office tower with a floor plan shaped like a bank's logo.
intruders.why: Named for its 42 storeys; its address is 25 Old Broad Street. The numeral looks like a street number.

intruders.title: Two International Finance Centre
intruders.description: Hong Kong office tower with a crown of tapering fins on the harbourfront.
intruders.why: The second tower of the IFC complex; its address is 8 Finance Street.

intruders.title: Taipei 101
intruders.description: Taiwanese tower of stacked flaring segments like bamboo joints.
intruders.why: Named for its 101 floors; its address is No. 7, Section 5, Xinyi Road.

theme: Architectural elements whose job is to carry or resist structural loads.
decoy: Named parts of classical and Gothic buildings

members.title: Flying buttress
members.description: Arched stone strut springing from a pier outside a nave wall.

members.title: Keystone
members.description: Wedge-shaped block at the crown of an arch.

members.title: Lintel
members.description: Horizontal beam across the top of a door or window opening.

members.title: Pendentive
members.description: Curved triangle of masonry between a dome and the square room beneath.

members.title: Squinch
members.description: Small arch or niche across the upper corner of a square room.

members.title: Corbel
members.description: Stone bracket projecting from a wall.

members.title: Voussoir
members.description: Tapered stone forming one of the units of an arch.

members.title: Caryatid
members.description: Sculpted draped female figure standing in place of a column.

members.title: Tie beam
members.description: Horizontal timber joining the feet of a pair of roof rafters.

intruders.title: Gargoyle
intruders.description: Carved grotesque creature projecting from the upper wall of a church.
intruders.why: A water spout that throws rain clear of the walls; it bears no structural load. Its place on buttresses and parapets makes it look structural.

intruders.title: Acroterion
intruders.description: Statue or ornament set on a plinth at the apex or corner of a pediment.
intruders.why: Purely decorative crowning ornament. It sits on the roofline like a structural finial.

theme: Structures deliberately aligned so that the sun lines up with them on a particular day of the year.
decoy: Monuments and places famous for dramatic sunrise or sunset views

members.title: Newgrange
members.description: Neolithic passage mound in Ireland's Boyne Valley with a roof-box above its entrance.

members.title: Stonehenge
members.description: Ring of standing sarsens and bluestones on Salisbury Plain.

members.title: Maeshowe
members.description: Chambered Neolithic cairn on Orkney with a long entrance passage.

members.title: Chankillo
members.description: Hilltop ruin in coastal Peru with a row of thirteen stone towers.

members.title: Karnak
members.description: Vast Egyptian temple complex of Amun-Re at Luxor with a great hypostyle hall.

members.title: Goseck circle
members.description: Neolithic ring ditch and palisade enclosure in Saxony-Anhalt.

members.title: Bryn Celli Ddu
members.description: Neolithic passage tomb on Anglesey, a grassy mound over a stone chamber.

members.title: Anthem Veterans Memorial
members.description: Five white pillars with elliptical openings in Anthem, Arizona.

intruders.title: Manhattan street grid
intruders.description: Long, straight crosstown streets of the Manhattan grid, laid out in 1811.
intruders.why: The 1811 grid was tilted about 29 degrees to fit the island, not the sun. The famous 'Manhattanhenge' sunsets are a coincidence.

intruders.title: MIT Infinite Corridor
intruders.description: Long main hallway running straight through a complex of MIT buildings.
intruders.why: Its 'MIThenge' sunset alignment in January and November was not intended by its designers.

theme: Landmarks that stand today largely as faithful rebuildings of an original that was destroyed.
decoy: Historic landmarks of Europe and Japan

members.title: Dresden Frauenkirche
members.description: Baroque Lutheran church with a bell-shaped stone dome on the Neumarkt.

members.title: Campanile di San Marco
members.description: Brick bell tower with a green pyramidal spire on St Mark's Square in Venice.

members.title: Kinkaku-ji
members.description: Kyoto temple pavilion covered in gold leaf above a mirror pond.

members.title: Stoa of Attalos
members.description: Two-story colonnaded hall on the edge of the Agora of Athens.

members.title: Cloth Hall, Ypres
members.description: Long Gothic trading hall with a belfry in a Flemish market town.

members.title: Monte Cassino Abbey
members.description: Benedictine hilltop monastery between Rome and Naples.

members.title: Warsaw Old Town Market Place
members.description: Square of colorful merchant houses at the heart of Poland's capital.

members.title: La Fenice
members.description: Venetian opera house where many Verdi operas premiered.

intruders.title: Ponte Vecchio
intruders.description: Medieval Florentine bridge lined with jewelers' shops over the Arno.
intruders.why: The only Florence bridge the retreating Germans spared in 1944; its fabric is largely 14th-century. Its neighbors were rebuilt.

intruders.title: Cologne Cathedral
intruders.description: Twin-spired Gothic church beside the main railway station on the Rhine.
intruders.why: Hit many times by bombs in World War II but never destroyed; it was repaired, not rebuilt. The city around it was flattened.

theme: Houses that architects designed for themselves to live in.
decoy: Celebrated houses by famous architects

members.title: Glass House
members.description: Transparent steel and glass pavilion on a lawn in New Canaan, Connecticut.

members.title: Eames House
members.description: Steel-framed house of colored panels in Pacific Palisades, Los Angeles.

members.title: Gehry Residence
members.description: Santa Monica bungalow wrapped in chain-link and corrugated metal.

members.title: Casa Luis Barragan
members.description: Mexico City house of bright walls and a stair without a handrail.

members.title: Sir John Soane's Museum
members.description: London townhouse crammed with antiquities and an Egyptian sarcophagus.

members.title: Horta Museum
members.description: Brussels Art Nouveau townhouse with whiplash ironwork and a glass-roofed stair.

members.title: Taliesin West
members.description: Desert compound of stone-studded concrete walls in Scottsdale, Arizona.

members.title: Muuratsalo Experimental House
members.description: Lakeside summer house in Finland with a courtyard of test brick patterns.

intruders.title: Farnsworth House
intruders.description: Glass-walled steel pavilion raised above a floodplain in Illinois.
intruders.why: Mies van der Rohe designed it as a weekend retreat for Dr. Edith Farnsworth and never lived there. It inspired Johnson's Glass House.

intruders.title: Villa Savoye
intruders.description: White villa on slender pilotis with a roof garden at Poissy near Paris.
intruders.why: Le Corbusier designed it for the Savoye family as a country house.

intruders.title: Villa Mairea
intruders.description: Finnish country house of timber and brick with a sinuous pool.
intruders.why: Alvar Aalto designed it for Harry and Maire Gullichsen. Aalto's own summer house is at Muuratsalo.

theme: Bridges built to replace a predecessor on the same route that had collapsed.
decoy: Road and rail bridges with notable engineering histories

members.title: Tacoma Narrows Bridge
members.description: Road crossing over Puget Sound in Washington State, opened in 1950.

members.title: Tay Bridge
members.description: Long railway crossing of the Firth of Tay at Dundee, opened in 1887.

members.title: I-35W Saint Anthony Falls Bridge
members.description: Concrete interstate crossing of the Mississippi in Minneapolis, opened in 2008.

members.title: Silver Memorial Bridge
members.description: Road crossing of the Ohio River near Point Pleasant, West Virginia, opened in 1969.

members.title: Genoa-Saint George Bridge
members.description: Steel viaduct over the Polcevera valley designed by Renzo Piano.

members.title: Sunshine Skyway Bridge
members.description: Yellow-cabled crossing of Tampa Bay in Florida, opened in 1987.

members.title: Seongsu Bridge
members.description: Steel truss crossing of the Han River in Seoul.

members.title: Tjorn Bridge
members.description: Cable-stayed road crossing on Sweden's west coast, opened in 1981.

intruders.title: London Millennium Footbridge
intruders.description: Steel pedestrian crossing over the Thames between St Paul's and Tate Modern.
intruders.why: Closed two days after its 2000 opening because it swayed, then fitted with dampers and reopened in 2002. It never collapsed and replaced nothing.

intruders.title: Forth Bridge
intruders.description: Red cantilever railway crossing of the Firth of Forth, opened in 1890.
intruders.why: The first bridge on its route. Thomas Bouch's suspension design for it was dropped after his Tay Bridge fell, which is why it gets linked to the disaster.

theme: Structures whose main form is a hyperboloid or hyperbolic paraboloid, curved surfaces that can be built entirely from straight members.
decoy: Striking curved towers and thin-shell roofs

members.title: Shukhov Tower
members.description: Latticework radio tower of crisscrossing steel in Moscow's Shabolovka district.

members.title: Kobe Port Tower
members.description: Red lattice observation tower on Kobe's waterfront, pinched at the waist.

members.title: Canton Tower
members.description: Slender twisting lattice-clad tower in Guangzhou.

members.title: Cathedral of Brasilia
members.description: Crown of sixteen bowed concrete columns with glass between them.

members.title: McDonnell Planetarium
members.description: Thin concrete shell in St. Louis's Forest Park.

members.title: Los Manantiales
members.description: Flower-shaped thin concrete shell restaurant at Xochimilco, Mexico City.

members.title: St. Mary's Cathedral, San Francisco
members.description: Church whose roof rises from a square base to a cross of stained glass.

members.title: Scotiabank Saddledome
members.description: Calgary arena with a saddle-shaped concrete roof.

intruders.title: Kresge Auditorium
intruders.description: Thin concrete shell auditorium at MIT resting on three points.
intruders.why: Its roof is one-eighth of a sphere, a curved surface that contains no straight lines. It is a famous thin shell from the same era.

intruders.title: Palazzetto dello Sport
intruders.description: Ribbed thin concrete shell arena in Rome ringed by Y-shaped buttresses.
intruders.why: Nervi's ribbed dome is a shallow spherical shell, not a ruled surface. It is a classic thin-shell structure.
